correctness.rationale: A dominated adjacent palette is removed by an explicit color-preserving bounded morphism. On a reduced chain, the recursive box formulas isolate each suffix and thereby each cluster, proving bisimulation minimality up to duplicate colors. A root bisimulation between two reduced suffixes then yields an ordered color-preserving isomorphism, hence equal reduced words and colors. The last retained level must be the final cluster; the converse placement construction realizes exactly the feasible palette words. Finite-model modal separation turns every subset of rooted types into a term operation. The verifier independently checks 42 feasible-language cases, 27 all-valuations cross-model bisimulation partitions and eight full term closures. All quantifiers, the zero-variable boundary and orientation examples were checked.

value.rationale: A full, natural modal-algebra clone invariant is determined for every positive ordered capacity vector, not an arbitrarily sliced numerical example. The formula distinguishes ordered three-world frames with identical cardinality by their 256 versus 64 unary term counts and yields a closed 4^h unary formula on arbitrary singleton chains. The proof identifies the precise quotient language that makes the computation possible, useful for finite modal expressiveness and local tabularity calculations.
